title: Two owner-approved in-place copper fixes: (A) reroute /poe/LED_Y_A out of the 57 V tap pocket; (B) widen every track below JLC's 0.1016 mm minimum
authority: H4 checkpoint, owner APPROVED. Decision was explicitly NO REBUILD: the board keeps its P6 placement and P7 routing, and anything needing a new footprint becomes a deferred open item instead.

cluster_A.title: Reroute /poe/LED_Y_A out of the 57 V tap pocket - 217 pairs at 0.2031 mm against a 0.600 mm requirement
cluster_A.authority: Owner: 'do the part that does not need a component. Reroute LED_Y_A out of the tap pocket, which closes the 217-pair geometry issue physically and makes the IPC-row argument moot.'
cluster_A.why_it_matters_more_than_the_number: /poe/LED_Y_A has exactly TWO pads: J1 pin 17 and R7 pin 2. R7 is a 330 ohm 0603 whose pin 1 is on +3V3. So the failure product of this gap is 57 V injected onto +3V3 through 330 ohm, unclamped - and +3V3 leaves the board on J3 pins 12 and 14 to every daughter board. There is no PESD device on any LED net (D31/D32/D40/D41/D42 are all on expansion signals; D10 TPD4E1U06 clamps only the MDI). A +3V3 clamp needs a new part and is therefore DEFERRED, which is exactly why the geometric fix has to land.

measured_now.population: 17 of 36 LED_Y_A segments against 21 of 27 POE_TAP_A2 F.Cu segments, 0.2031-0.5071 mm, over roughly 10 mm of parallel run

cluster_A.target: >= 0.635 mm from /poe/LED_Y_A copper to ALL FOUR /poe/POE_TAP_* nets, on every layer, for EVERY pair - not just the worst. 0.635 mm is the board-wide adopted figure (TPS2378 datasheet layout section) and ICD-01 rev A6 s5.1 is explicit that the 0.13 mm B4 coated column is NOT claimed, so do not design to 0.13 mm.
guidance: The clean solution is almost certainly TOPOLOGICAL, not a nudge: LED_Y_A currently runs ~10 mm parallel to POE_TAP_A2 inside J1's tap pocket. Take it OUT of the pocket - drop to an inner layer or B.Cu for the transit and come back up, or route it around the far side of J1's land. LED_Y_A carries about 10 mA to an indicator LED, so it is electrically free to move: any layer, any detour, extra vias are fine.

Check /poe/LED_G_A, /poe/LED_Y_C and /poe/LED_G_C in the same pocket while you are there and report their minimum to the taps too. A previous fixer found that the reported worst pair hid 216 siblings on this very net pair, so measure the whole population, not the minimum.

Do NOT solve this by moving any POE_TAP copper. The taps were brought to 0.6502 mm (tap-to-tap) and 0.639-1.770 mm (tap-to-SHIELD) earlier in P8 at real cost, and a new DRU rule poe_tap_differential_pair (0.60 mm) plus magjack_isolation_barrier (1.30 mm) now hold those lines. Breaking either is a regression.
Do NOT move any footprint. J1 and R7 are both in placement.fixed and the board is fully routed.

cluster_B.title: 189 tracks at 0.1000 mm against JLC's 0.1016 mm minimum - widen them
cluster_B.authority: Owner: 'Fix the 189 DFM track-width errors in place. Tracks are 0.1000 mm against JLC's 0.1016 mm minimum - a 1.6 um gap. Widen them via route_edit.'
cluster_B.measured_now: gate dfm reports 194 errors, of which 189 are 'trace width 0.1000 mm below JLC minimum 0.1016 mm' - 136 on F.Cu, 53 on B.Cu. Also present and NOT yours: 3 copper-clearance and 2 hole-to-hole errors.
cluster_B.root_cause_for_context_only: board_init writes min_track_width: 0.1 into the .kicad_pro, below EVERY JLC profile, and this board's hand-written .kicad_dru contains none of rules_gen's generated floors. So DRC never objected. The orchestrator is raising the floor to 0.1016 mm separately - do not edit the .kicad_pro or .kicad_dru yourself.
cluster_B.target: No track anywhere on the board below 0.1016 mm. Widen to 0.110 mm where there is room, so the result is not sitting exactly on the fab limit; fall back to 0.1016 mm where 0.110 does not fit; report any track that cannot reach even 0.1016 mm with its measured available room and blocker.
guidance: There IS room: work/p8/residual_report.json measured these same +3V3 escape tracks as having 0.291-0.316 mm of widening headroom against a 0.5 mm requirement, so 0.110 mm is comfortable for the great majority.

CRITICAL route_edit MECHANIC: route_edit applies ALL adds BEFORE ALL removes, and dedups adds on geometry within 0.001 mm. Widening a track at UNCHANGED geometry therefore needs TWO SEPARATE route_edit invocations - remove first, then add - or the add is silently skipped as a duplicate, the remove then deletes the original, and the whole file rolls back. Widening in one file 'works' only because width is part of the track key; do not rely on that at 189 items. Batch it, and verify the applied count each time.
Work in batches of 30-50 with a DRC run after each. If a batch regresses, bisect it rather than abandoning it.

Some of these 0.100 mm tracks are ALSO in the check_current undersized_track set. Widening them to 0.110 mm will not clear check_current (it wants 0.5 mm) and that is fine and expected - do not chase it.

oracle: gate.py --gate drc_routed <board> must read total 0 (err+warn 0) after EVERY batch. gate place and check_decoupling are STRUCTURALLY BLIND to routed copper - on this board a 0.300 mm placement nudge passed both and still introduced a SHORTING_ITEMS. DRC is the only oracle. Refill with `kc.py drc --refill --save-board` after any plane-crossing edit, then run the gate.
hard_rules: NEVER pass --commit to gate.py, and run NO git command at all - the repo is shared with two paused board runs.

Do not write board edits from heredoc-inlined python; a permission classifier blocks heredoc writes. Write helper .py files with the file-editing tool, then run them. All board writes go through route_edit.py.
Do not move any footprint. Do not edit constraints.json, the .kicad_pro or the .kicad_dru.
Do not touch the owner-accepted waivers: 94 check_current, the 10 package-internal check_creepage items, 11 check_return_path, 2 check_decoupling. Do not make any of them worse.
The 25 MHz oscillator island (Y10, C30, C31, R35, R36 and nets /eth/XI, /eth/XO, /eth/XO_XTAL) was just re-placed and re-routed by another agent. Do not touch it.
